digest.component_or_area: code-review gate model-class wiring and usage log
propositions: Per-step model class declarations in code-review.yaml are silently ignored; all LLM calls run on the single resolved cfg.model instead of their declared frontier/standard classes.
The usage log records only the prompt name (op) and cannot attribute a call to a specific step, since the code-review-base prompt is used by both the base step and the round_a/round_b batch finder.

Step 0 adds a ContextVar carrying the step id and raw declared class token, set by the step executor and read at runner.py:547, so record() can additively write step and model_class (only when the token is in CLASS_NAMES).
The plan-review gate honors classes because it wraps run_workflow in gate_config(cfg), while the code-review dispatch path omits that scope; the true broken seam is not yet confirmed.
An offline end-to-end test with a fake runner injected beneath the production RunnerAgentStep must assert each of five steps receives its declared class and must be RED on current code.
The verify step's pre-existing model: standard declaration is a pre-existing defect, not a regression, and must be shown honored by the same test.
